findings.reason: §6 makes landing the only thing that releases a downstream request, so a commitless upstream (an investigate or docs-only node, which promotion accepts) either strands its waiters with no obligation raised or releases them before its work is on the branch; one sentence must say which.
findings.text: §8 defines landed as "that row's recorded head commit is an ancestor of the project's primary branch", but the row's revision is written only when `promoted_revision` is non-empty (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:1479-1480`) and the comment there states a run that "asserted no code leaves the key absent"; `_promoted_revision` otherwise falls back to the worktree's `HEAD` (`reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:294-314`), which for a commitless run is the base commit and is already an ancestor — so a `no_commit` promotion either never satisfies the test or satisfies it at promotion, before any merge, and s8's claim that ancestry "is the fact that changes when `crew land` merges" is false for it

findings.reason: the row's field exists (`promoted_revision`, `reckon/crew/promotion.py:1480`) and `sweep_promoted_revisions` (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:1985`) already answers exactly this ancestry question; naming them tightens the node but the capability and the measure are unchanged.
findings.text: §8 says the landed test reads "that row's recorded head commit" through the row "read through the public `run_ids`", but `run_ids` (`reckon/ledger.py:1019`) returns only id membership without decoding a row, so the sentence names a reader for a fact it cannot supply

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every anchor resolves: `parse_plan_ref` (`reckon/_schema.py:276`), `_readiness_rows` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1056`), `_readiness_by_slug` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:3094`, which does keep only one verdict per plan), `parse_manifest`/`MANIFEST_STATUSES`/`TERMINAL_MANIFEST_STATUSES` (`reckon/crew/reports.py:126-139`, `:317`), `promotion.py`, `run_ids` (`reckon/ledger.py:1019`), and `TaskNode` (`reckon/crew/node.py:725`). `RUN_DELIVERED_STATUSES` is exactly `("complete", "completed", "done", "landed", "promoted")`, and the four non-`complete` members are the words `MANIFEST_STATUSES` excludes, as s8 states.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — s8's measure is a set of chain, cycle and closure arms each of which can fail on its own, and it names a declared negative control ("The negative arm declares B's §2 done before queuing, and the request goes straight to `queued`") so the wait is shown to be what held the request rather than a blanket refusal.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — s8 names write paths in `reckon/` and a new test file only; it cites no scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — s8 proposes no symbol carrying a plan label, stage name or ticket number; the one new shared function and the per-section predicate are described by what they do.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the landed definition has no branch for a promoted run that asserts no commit, so the ancestry test does not decide landed for it.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the union of waits, the cycle refusal, the readiness assembly and the delivered-status narrowing all serve one goal: a queued request respects the work's DAG across plans and projects.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` gives s8 only `a-queue-holds-the-whole-plan#s2`, which is the section that adds `_readiness_rows` and `RUN_DELIVERED_STATUSES`; both are present in the tree (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1056`, `:1023`), and no other section owns a symbol s8 relies on.
